behavioral_effects: None stated. An empty list is a claim that nothing observably changes.
compatibility_impact: Discovery behavior is identical: Traefik reads the same labels through tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375. depends_on uses service_started so a failing proxy healthcheck degrades discovery rather than blocking the edge from starting. Applies on the next prod deploy (docker compose up recreates traefik and adds the proxy); until then the host keeps the old wiring. compose-check including the prod tail passes; the standalone compose-check-prod target still requires the interpolation dummies it always required.
reason: Security finding: production mounts /var/run/docker.sock into Traefik with the insecure API enabled; a read-only bind mount does not restrict the Docker API itself, so a Traefik compromise reaches full host control. A socket proxy with a container-read-only endpoint allowlist bounds that blast radius
rollback: git revert restores the direct socket mount; the socket-proxy container and docker-socket network are removed on the next compose up --remove-orphans.
security_impact: Traefik no longer holds the Docker socket. A digest-pinned tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy (v0.5.0) owns the read-only mount on an internal no-egress network shared only with Traefik, and exposes CONTAINERS=1 plus the ping/version defaults; verified locally against the pinned image: container and label listing ALLOWED, container create, image list, and exec all DENIED. A Traefik compromise now reads container metadata instead of reaching the full Docker API (the previous :ro mount only made the socket file read-only, not the API). The insecure dashboard API remains loopback-bound on the host, unchanged and out of scope here.
summary: Put a least-privilege socket proxy between Traefik and the Docker API
